sample_unit: responses (11 surgeon, 11 LLM) to one standardized acute DVT vignette

links.outcome: Readability of patient-directed DVT explanations from LLMs versus surgeons using Spanish readability indices
links.effect: LLM responses were more readable on three of four indices (all p<0.02); Crawford grade 5.4 vs 6.1 (p=0.075). LLM responses were longer (903 vs 354 words).
links.quote: Current-generation LLMs matched board-certified surgeons in clinical completeness and produced more readable, descriptively far more consistent patient-facing explanations, without the communication failures observed in a minority of human responses.

links.outcome: Educational grade level required to read LLM versus surgeon patient explanations
links.effect: LLM responses required a numerically lower grade level (Crawford 5.4 vs 6.1; p=0.075); one surgeon response fell far outside the interpretable range.
links.quote: LLM responses were more readable on three of four content-complexity indices (Fernández-Huerta, Gutiérrez de Polini, Szigriszt-Pazos; all p < 0.02) and required a numerically lower educational grade level (Crawford 5.4 vs 6.1; p = 0.075).

screen.reason: The study empirically compares patient-directed explanations for acute DVT generated by LLMs versus board-certified vascular surgeons using clinical appropriateness and readability metrics, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
